resources.string: On-device malware, app, link, and background protection
File and link scanning use a signed threat database. Updates are accepted only after cryptographic verification.
Choose a file to start scanning.
The SHA-256 fingerprint is not in the active threat database.
This APK is not in the active database. This does not prove that it is safe.
The file name uses a misleading double extension.
The SHA-256 fingerprint matches a known signature in the active database.
This is the standard harmless anti-malware test signature.
The file could not be scanned.
Files, installed-app scan data, and scanned links stay on the device. Internet access is used only for signed threat-database updates.
File indicators: %1$s • Link indicators: %2$s • APK identity indicators: %3$s

A clean result only means no known signature was found. It is not a guarantee that a file is safe.
Review user-installed apps using local threat signatures, requested permissions, install source, accessibility services, and package fingerprints.

To perform this security scan, Aman Security reads the installed app list, requested permissions, install source, accessibility-service declarations, and local package fingerprints. This information stays on this device and is not uploaded.
Run a scan to review user-installed apps.
Scanned: %1$s • Needs review: %2$s • High-risk indicators: %3$s • Known threats: %4$s
Installed-app scan could not be completed.
No elevated indicators were found in the user-installed apps scanned.
Permission and behavior indicators provide security context; by themselves they do not prove that an app is malicious.
Installed outside a recognized app store or source could not be verified
No elevated permission or install-source indicators.

Aman will encrypt the selected file inside private app storage, verify its SHA-256 again, and remove the original only if the provider allows deletion. If removal is not possible, quarantine is cancelled.
The file changed after the scan. It was not quarantined. Scan it again before taking action.
The encrypted copy was discarded because the original file could not be removed. The file remains in its original location.
Quarantine could not be completed. The original file was not intentionally removed.
Quarantined files are encrypted with a device-protected key and kept in private app storage. Restore or permanently delete them only when you choose.
Restoring makes the file accessible outside quarantine again. Choose a destination only if you understand the original detection.
The file was restored and removed from quarantine.
Restore was stopped because the restored data did not match the stored SHA-256. The quarantined copy was kept.
The file could not be restored. The quarantined copy was kept.
This removes the encrypted quarantined copy and cannot be undone.
The quarantined file was deleted permanently.
The quarantined file could not be deleted.
Exclusions apply only to the exact SHA-256 you approve. A matching known-threat result is still shown; the exclusion only suppresses the quarantine recommendation for that exact hash.
Add this exact hash to exclusions?
Use exclusions only for files you trust. Aman will continue to display the underlying detection, but will not recommend quarantine for this exact SHA-256 until you remove the exclusion.
The exact file hash was added to exclusions.
A bounded local history of file scan results. It stays on this device and can be cleared at any time.
This removes saved scan-history records. It does not delete quarantined files or exclusions.
Scan a web link locally before opening it. Aman checks signed link indicators and combines several phishing-risk signals without treating any single heuristic as proof.
Paste or type a web link
Enter a link or share one to Aman Security.
Only valid web links using the standard web protocols can be scanned.
The normalized link is not in the active link-indicator database and no elevated combination of local indicators was found. This does not guarantee that the site is safe.
A cryptographic link or host fingerprint matches the active signed threat database.
This reserved test link verifies the link-detection path without directing you to a malicious site.
Uses a numeric network address instead of a domain name
Uses an internationalized encoded domain label
Contains user-information syntax before the host, which can disguise the real destination
Uses an unusually deep subdomain chain
Contains account, verification, payment, or login-related wording
Link scanning is on-device. The link is not sent to Aman or to a third-party lookup service.
You can also use the Android Share menu on a text link and choose Aman Security.

A signed package-identity threat indicator matched the active database.

Code-pattern inspection reached its local safety limit. Manifest, certificate, and package-identity checks are still shown.

Several independent APK indicators combined to a high review score. This does not prove malware by itself.
The file uses an APK extension, but Android package metadata could not be parsed. Treat the archive as untrusted until its source is verified.
The package name or signing-certificate fingerprint matches a signed threat indicator, even though the file SHA-256 may differ.
Static analysis never runs the APK. It inspects package metadata, bounded archive structure, signing identity, and selected code markers locally on the device.
A safe signed package-identity test indicator matched. It is not a malware verdict.
When enabled, Aman scans user-installed or updated apps promptly and periodically checks new or changed files inside one folder you choose.
Protection is local and conservative. Aman never installs, opens, deletes, or quarantines automatically. Android may defer the battery-aware folder check; app-install scans are event driven.
Protection is enabled, but Android notification permission is off. Alerts remain in recent protection activity.
Last folder check: %1$s • New or changed files scanned: %2$s • Alerts: %3$s

Aman will locally inspect newly installed or updated user apps and, if you choose a folder, periodically inspect new or changed files in that folder. File and app inventories are not uploaded. Nothing is deleted or quarantined automatically. Android notification permission is used only for high-risk or known-threat alerts.
Access to the protected folder is no longer available. Choose the folder again to resume folder checks.
